notes: Spec defect 15 of this plan, and a new shape for the catalogue: not a requirement contradicting its own justification, but a FALSE FACTUAL CLAIM ABOUT THE TEST SUITE. The ticket asserted that no existing assertion covered an all-null array; _hand_built_data() builds a one-stage axis and one test stored values=[None], which is trivially all-None, so requirements 1 and 2 were logically incompatible with a pinned assertion. The specialist proved it by measurement before implementing anything and escalated. Amended as requirement 9. Lesson: a claim about an existing test is verifiable by running it, and neither refinement nor readiness scoring executes anything.

Guardian found one non-blocking gap the orchestrator then closed: requirement 3's negative direction (no INFO line for a chart that lost nothing) was correctly implemented but untested - mutating `if dropped:` to `if True:` passed all 504 tests. Closed with a drop-record assertion in the AC3 test, proven to fail under that exact mutation.

Orchestrator error worth recording: the first version of that assertion counted every INFO record of the payload logger, on the premise that _build_chart_entry was the module's only INFO caller. False - build_payload's timed-step helper in logging_setup emits 'Payload JSON construido' under this module's logger name. A grep for 'logger.' inside payload.py cannot see a record logged on the module's behalf from elsewhere. Fixed by matching the drop line's own message template.

Spec defect 16, amended before dispatch: (a) the DoD demanded test_renderer_contract.py pass unchanged while requirement 9 deletes the section that test_checklist_ends_with_ticket_028_placeholder_for_plant_filters asserts is present - a test encoding the precondition that this very ticket had not run; (b) requirement 9 numbered the new checklist steps from 19 when the last step is 20, because the refinement read the file before the epic-03 boundary inserted steps 7 and 18.

CROSS-TICKET COLLISION 4, and a new subtype: the collision is with a NON-VACUITY test rather than with a behavioural assertion. tests/test_charts_submarket.py mutates the FIRST occurrence of a literal via _remove_first and then requires the checker to raise. A second copy of closest("section.chart") or ".entity-selector" in dashboard.js therefore disarms the mutation. Resolved in code, not in the test: applyPlantFilter resolves the select and section via getElementById, and the new listener uses closest(".chart"). The guardian confirmed the looser selector is PROVABLY equivalent - the only element in the codebase carrying class="chart" is the <section> itself.

CORRECTION for the learnings: the specialist described that collision as the test 'passing vacuously'. It does not - it fails loudly with 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE AssertionError'. Verified by the orchestrator by appending a second literal to the asset and running the case, and confirmed independently by the guardian. The distinction matters: a test that breaks loudly is a far smaller risk class than one that silently stops discriminating, and recording one as the other would distort the lesson.

Two project-specific traps the specialist hit and fixed itself, both worth carrying forward: typing the Unicode combining range literally produced real combining characters in the asset (caught by isascii()); and a JS comment containing <section class="chart"> created a spurious 24th section for dashboard_document.py's slicing regex, because the asset is embedded VERBATIM in the document - a comment in the JavaScript is searchable text of the final HTML.

open_decisions_for_developer: Cost scale: FUTURO is about 2.3e8 while PRESENTE is about 5.9e4, so a shared linear bar axis renders PRESENTE invisible. Ticket-030 ships the grouped bars as specified and logs the spread; a log axis or a split chart is out of scope and needs a developer ruling.
Plant labels carry the name without the code. Adding the code is a one-line label change if the developer wants it.
output.decimals is global, not per chart. Deferred; no ticket owns it.

Resolved 2026-09-10 by the developer (epic-03 decision E3-1): the renderer is tested with Python-only assertions on the generated HTML and JSON plus a manual checklist under docs/. No JS engine and no Node toolchain (measured: node and npm are absent from this WSL environment). Resolved 2026-09-10 by the developer (epic-03 decision E3-2): the chart heading is always the curated ChartSpec.title; Registries.title_for supplies an additive subtitle or hover text where it differs. Measured against the real METADADOS_OPERACAO: the registry name is better where the curated title is an acronym (CMO, EARMF) but would collapse the hm3-versus-percent and afluente-versus-incremental distinctions that resolved master plan open questions 2 and 3.

Resolved 2026-09-10 by orchestrator ruling: URL-hash state shared by the deck selector and the level navigation is OUT OF SCOPE. The spec does not require linkable views, so refinement must not introduce hash routing. Reopen only on an explicit developer request.

Resolved 2026-09-11 (epic-04 decision E4-3): the plant payload stays FULLY EMBEDDED, because the deliverable is one self-contained offline HTML and any lazy fetch needs a server or sibling files. Size is managed by rounding to output.decimals, omitting entities whose arrays are entirely null, and ticket-032 measuring and warning. Lazy RENDERING already exists: ticket-023 renders only the active group. Refine 032 together with 027. Measured motivation: the epic-03 payload alone reaches about 56 MB at 30 decks times 3 scenarios, past the 50 MB default.

Resolved 2026-09-11 (epic-04 decision E4-4): filtering plants by submarket and by equivalent reservoir is OUT OF SCOPE. The spec asks for name and code filters only; the registry supports more, which is why it is tempting, but it is unrequested scope. Consistent with the epic-03 ruling on URL-hash state. Reopen only on explicit request.
